events.text:
This is a demo of a basic first-person shooter (FPS) type game.
[b]Controls:[/b] use arrow keys to move, and spacebar to shoot tomatoes.

[h3]How it works[/h3]
The game is basically a 2D shooter, but uses the 3D camera object to give it a first-person perspective. You can see it in a 2D perspective if you toggle the '2D camera' group to be enabled. The piggies use a Bullet behavior so they move around and bounce off solids, and the player can shoot tomatoes at them.

The piggies, tomatoes and puff when piggies disappear are all a kind of 'billboard', i.e. 2D sprites shown in 3D. To get this appearance in Construct, they use 3D rotation to make them stand upright relative to the floor, and then rotate them to face the camera so they always appear flat against the view. Collisions are managed with a separate collision sprite to have better control of the collision shape, and that shape also moves around - the billboard is attached as a child and acts solely as a visual representation of the object.

Note an important detail is all the 'billboard' objects are placed on their own layer named "Billboards", and the layer [b]Draw order[/b] is set to [b]Camera distance[/b]. This is to make sure transparency works correctly. A normal 2D drawing order could mean the transparent areas of nearby billboards obscure far away ones. The [i]Camera distance[/i] draw order means the billboards furthest away from the camera are drawn first, and nearest drawn last, ensuring everything appears correctly.

events.title: 3D camera
events.description: Enable this group to see the game from a first-person perspective.

children.text: Always set a 3D camera parallel to the layout with the position and angle of the Player sprite.

events.title: 2D camera
events.description: Enable this group to see the game from a top-down 2D perspective.

children.text: In 2D mode, restore a 2D camera view and then just scroll to the player normally. Also set the normally invisible collision shapes to be visible so the way the movement and collisions work in the game is more obvious.

events.title: General
events.description: Event blocks that implement the gameplay regardless of the type of view.

children.text: Always make the piggy objects look towards the player, for a billboard style appearance. Note that they use 3D rotation to stand up on the Y axis, and then 2D rotation to orient towards the camera.

Shoot tomatoes when pressing spacebar. Note the tomato has both a collision sprite for 2D movement and collision detection, and a billboard sprite attached for 3D display. The billboard is also slightly elevated on the Z axis so it comes out just below the player's viewpoint.

actions.text: Adjust the tomato movement angle by a small random amount so they spread out a little rather than form a perfectly straight line.

children.text: When a tomato collides with the scenery, destroy it. Note we only want tomatoes to collide with 3D shapes on the ground - they should ignore ones raised up with Z elevation, so you can still shoot tomatoes through the archway. Therefore also check that the 3D shape it collided with has a Z elevation of 0. Note the tomato billboard is in a hierarchy with the collision sprite and will automatically be destroyed as well.
When a tomato collides with a piggy (using the collision sprites), add to its hitcount, make it flash, and destroy the tomato.
The piggy billboard is a separate sprite attached as a child of the collision sprite, so pick the right one using a sub-event.
If a piggy gets hit by a tomato 5 times, destroy it and create a "puff" billboard in its place; as a disappearing animation, tween the opacity to 0 so it fades out.
